It's Time To Declare Peace
By Iain Young, who runs a Vancouver communications firm, has worked with several not-for-profit organizations on the issue of marijuana use. E-mail: iyoung@uniserve.com

It seems we can't turn on our TV sets or open our newspapers in British Columbia without being subjected to a bombardment of media coverage of police raids on marijuana-growing operations. We read strong statements from police all over the lower mainland about " cleaning out these operations. " Recently, a B.C. judge handed down a stiff sentence as a " deterrent " in one of these cases.
(MarijuanaNews note: The sentence was for two years, while the prosecutor had only asked for 4 months. This is very " stiff " by Canadian standards, and will not stand up on appeal, because Canadian law requires that every effort be made to avoid incarceration, especially for first time offenders, as was the defendant in this case.)

Predictably, The Vancouver Sun called this " the right thing to do. " Clearly, the provincial establishment is trying to pull together on this get-tough stance on marijuana.

But what do they think this hard line will accomplish, and how far would they like it to go?

In the United States, the use of what amounts to paramilitary police squads and mass incarceration programs with mandatory life sentences has already been tried. In the past 20 years, Washington's " war on drugs " has cost American taxpayers hundreds of billions of dollars. It has brought social disaster to hundreds of thousands of families, clogged courts and prisons, bankrolled organized crime by inflating drug prices, and caused widespread corruption among police departments. Yet it has not resulted in any decrease in the availability of drugs.
See
Marijuana Cases In 1998 Accounted For 33.9 Percent Of All Federal Drug Convictions

So, given this example, why are our media not asking the get-tough advocates in Canada what they think their proposals would actually achieve?

And why haven't the media given much serious consideration to what it is these police raids are trying to wipe out? Marijuana is one of the most intensively researched drugs in history. That research started in the 19th century with the British Commission on Indian Hemp,
See
One Writer Knows The Real Reason That UK Politicians Are Afraid Of A Royal Commission: It Will Say The Same Thing As The Indian Hemp Commission Report Under Queen Victoria. and has continued in Germany, Switzerland,
See
Swiss Upper House Approves Proposal to Legalize Marijuana Use
New Zealand,
See
A Major Contribution -- Regulate And Tax Cannabis --
Full Text of New Zealand Drug Policy Forum Final Report

the United States, Australia, the Netherlands, Britain and Canada.
See
Head of 1971 Canadian Commission Recommending Decriminalization of Marijuana
" Stands By Report "

All the major studies have concluded that, for most people, marijuana is relatively safe, non-addictive and not a gateway to more serious drug use. Indeed, we are now recognizing several beneficial medical effects from its reasonable use.
See
Is marijuana addictive?

So why are we continuing to criminalize tens of thousands of our citizens every year for using this generally safe, pleasant and beneficial plant? Well, here is the bottom line, and it is something that the media don't have the guts to say. The laws on marijuana are simply wrong. Wrong because they are not based on scientific research or any kind of social reality. Instead, we Canadians are being directed by the socially disastrous ideology of the American war on drugs.
See
Two Leading Canadian Anti-Prohibitionists Quoted
As Their Papers Actually Report On Canada’s Marijuana Arrest Statistics.
2 Amazing Articles

If we adopted an intelligent, effective and socially realistic approach to drug control, we would have to be willing to resist the political pressures that would be brought to bear on Canada by the war-on-drugs interests in the United States. The war on drugs is not only unjust and uneconomic, it is unwinnable. The Americans have proved that. Arresting, fining and imprisoning thousands of Canadians to please the Americans by going along with their inhuman, corrupt and socially bankrupt fantasy is not a good idea.

So let's start asking our guardians of freedom in the media to stop going along for the ride on this issue. It's time they found the courage to ask our politicians intelligent and honest questions about the future of the war on drugs. It's time our politicians found the courage to give us honest intelligent answers.

See
Great Critiques Of Media Bias In Reporting On Marijuana From News Watch Ezine -- Two Articles

Section: Your view
By Richard Barszczewski
MARIJUANA ANYTHING BUT A SAFE DRUG -- COP

Should the laws that keep marijuana illegal go up in smoke?

Even a cursory scroll through the Internet will load you down with volumes of opinions, particularly from those who view marijuana as a harmless substance, a sort of '60s joke you don't have to take too seriously, so let's just make it legal.

The simple fact is marijuana isn't harmless.
See
Is marijuana really harmless, like everyone has been saying?

There's overwhelming agreement among medical and scientific experts that the strength and addictive powers of today's " B.C. bud " are more powerful than the 1960's version.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is simply a lie. First, there is no data from the 1960’s. Second, the average potency today is essentially the same as it was 20 years ago.)
See
Potent Pot Myth Undermined By Report From The Ultimate Authority. Cited By Swedish Prohibitionist Who Don’t Seem To Understand. As Usual.
and
UN Nark Prohibitionist Propaganda Organization Issues Annual Report; Uses Potent Pot Line To Justify More Marijuana Prohibition

The number of young people receiving treatment for marijuana addiction grows yearly. In face of all the casual attitudes towards marijuana, it's important to let our youth know that marijuana will negatively impact their lives.
See
The Real Data On Teen Marijuana " Abuse Treatment " – What The Media Don’t Tell Us:
" Half of marijuana treatment admissions were referred through the criminal justice system. "
-- Analysis By Richard Cowan

Motor vehicle accidents are the No. 1 killer of young people, even when sober. Add in marijuana use, alcohol or other drugs and the combination is deadly.
See
Canadian Study Confirms That Marijuana Impairs Driving Far Less Than Alcohol
and
1994 Dutch Study On " Marijuana Use And Driving " In Real World Conditions

The pro-legalization movement tries to convince us that marijuana is a harmless social activity and that people should be able to smoke it without fear of the law.
(MarijuanaNews note: Those are two entirely different points.)

Meanwhile, doctors and scientists say smoking it may cause serious health problems. If it's starting to sound like the debate around tobacco, well, there are similarities.

The manner in which marijuana is produced today (residential grow ops) poses unique hazards; the majority of these grow operations are now controlled by organized criminal gangs motivated to make a fast dollar regardless of risk to themselves or neighbors.
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me, but what is the parallel with tobacco? Is tobacco grown indoors by organized crime? Notice that this is a cost of marijuana prohibition being passed off as a danger of marijuana.)
See
Organized Crime In The Marijuana Trade.
Why More " Law Enforcement " is Counterproductive.
An Excellent Halifax Editorial Says, " Marijuana laws encourage crime. "

Some of the costs to the public associated with marijuana grow operations include fighting fires (due to electrical wiring and heating equipment), thefts of power (electrical by-passes) and an increase in household insurance premiums to cover the high costs of restoring rental properties after they've been trashed by an operation.
(MarijuanaNews note: Again, these are costs of marijuana prohibition.)

Individuals who actively promote legalization say these problems would disappear if marijuana was legalized. That legalization and/or regulating it somehow would remove it from criminals, cause prices to fall and eliminate the black market. Well, alcohol and tobacco are legal and regulated. Yet both are sold on the black market by organized gangs, both cost the government more in health costs than the revenue taxes from selling them, and both are more widely abused than marijuana. Would regulating marijuana be any different?
(MarijuanaNews note: That is bizarre. Are the alcohol and tobacco trades in Canada really controlled by organized crime? If so, why don’t we hear about raids on illegal stills and tobacco grow ops?)
See
The Reality Of the Marijuana Situation In Canada: Unequal Injustice.
Alcohol Costs Canadian Health Almost 100 Times As Much As Marijuana.
Tobacco: Almost 200 As Much – Article and Editorial
and
Great London Times Column and News From New Zealand Compare Marijuana and Alcohol
and
A Proposal For A Rational Allocation Of Drug Education Budgets
Based On The Harm Done By Various Substances -- Analysis By Richard Cowan

We believe there's a real need to crack down on traffickers and to inform the public.

Helping our kids make good choices starts by giving them real facts, the kind with medical and scientific credibility.
See
The Need For Drug Prohibition Education.
Analysis By Richard Cowan.
How Can Parents Tell Their Children The Truth In A Sea Of Lies About Marijuana?

As a parent and officer, I know when you strip away marijuana's thin veneer of social acceptability and replace it with the medical truth, making the right decision about use or legalization is pretty easy.

We all talk about our young people as our most precious resource. If that's the case then it's incumbent on all of us to protect them by giving them the facts. After all, awareness, education and prevention are the key to making healthy choices that last a lifetime.
See
How the War On Marijuana To Save The Children
Has Become A War On the Children To Save Marijuana Prohibition

For more information call the RCMP Drug Awareness at (604) 264-3029. Richard Barszczewski is Inspector, Officer in Charge Drug Intelligence and Field Operations, RCMP " E " Division
See
As Canadian Senate Gets Ready To Study Prohibition, Canadian Police Push Prohibitionist Propaganda At Taxpayer Expense. 4 Items

(MarijuanaNews note: Any American who spends a little time in Canada will be amused and embarrassed to discover that there is a whole genre of Canadian humor based on American ignorance about Canada. On the other hand, Canadians cannot escape knowing more than they want to know about their huge neighbor.

This makes the arguments advanced by some Canadians for higher marijuana penalties all the more puzzling.

As Iain Young points out, " Arresting, fining and imprisoning thousands of Canadians to please the Americans by going along with their inhuman, corrupt and socially bankrupt fantasy is not a good idea. "

That is an understatement!

According to the DEA, half of the marijuana consumed in DEAland is grown there, so draconian penalties clearly do not keep high prices from drawing people into cultivation. The penalties simply help maintain prices that are an incentive to risk taking.

As Young says, " Canadians are being directed by the socially disastrous ideology of the American war on drugs. "

MarijuanaNews is devoted to the arguments for the legalization of marijuana, so there is no need for more reinforcement of that argument here, but that is not the same thing as explaining how the Canadians in particular can get from here to there.

When Australia or New Zealand legalize, DEAland will undoubtedly scream loudly and bring pressure, but their geographic isolation will prevent their actions having any direct impact on other countries, and -- even more important -- it will keep other countries marijuana prohibition from having an impact on them.

See
Why the US won't let Australia reform its drug laws. The real drug war. Background for IoS Article See: Independent on Sunday THE DRUGS WORLD WAR - WHAT WENT WRONG? By DAVID MARR ...

However Canada is next door to the world’s largest marijuana market and the nuclear busy-body, which means that Canada will be under much more pressure.
See
Run For Your Lives! " US Says Drugs, Terror Pouring In From Canada "!
Or, The Problems Of Living Next To A Superpower Run By Narcs.

We read a lot about the problems in Mexico and Colombia caused by DEAland prohibition, although they are usually not described in that way. However, some part of the boom in indoor marijuana growing in Canada is supported by DEAland demand. How much, is a matter of conjecture.

See
RCMP Report On Marijuana Trafficking Contradicts The Party Line
About Marijuana Smuggling From Canada To DEAland. Far More Goes North Than South

Nonetheless, there really will be problems in Canada unless growing is fully legalized and licensed. This makes the usual transition through " decriminalization " more difficult for them.

If the Canadian police turn a blind eye to all marijuana cultivation, as they should, then even more people will start growing for the huge DEAland market and the narcocracy will scream even louder and bring even more pressure on Ottawa to crack down.

See
Someone Floats A Rumor That DEAland Wants To Blacklist Canada;
Washington Denies Everything, But Canadian Prohibitionists Seem To Cheer,
Sort Of… 3 Articles
and
US Narks Teach Mounties How To Violate The Rights of Their Citizens

Of course, as the above piece from the RCMP nark demonstrates, they will have plenty of support from Canadian prohibitionists.
See
" Enforcers Challenge Cannabis Liberation Movement " In Canada – Great Journalism!!!

There is one interim step that the Canadian national and provincial governments could take that would reduce the problems of marijuana prohibition that the Canadian narks try to blame on marijuana.

The current Vancouver policy of de facto decriminalization of marijuana possession could be extended to small scale growing – perhaps 100 plants – in a person’s own home, or rented home with the permission of the owner -- and when the electricity is being paid for, not stolen from the electric company. Outdoor growing would be similarly tolerated.

Dutch style coffee shops could be tolerated with approved growers supplying them.

With these steps, the growers would not be afraid to call the police if they feel threaten by thieves. Nor would they have any need steal electricity or to hide cash. They would probably even pay taxes on some of their income, although this would be a secondary benefit.

Naturally, a lot of this almost-legal Canadian marijuana would inevitably be smuggled across the border. Aside from the DEAland prohibitionist zeal to interfere in Canadian internal affairs, the smuggling would lead to legally sound but morally bankrupt complaints from DEAland.

The Canadian police could cooperate with the DEAland customs and border police to try to stop this traffic, but the Canadians should make very clear that these problems are caused by DEAland marijuana prohibition, not by Canadian freedom.

It still will not be easy for them to escape from the marijuana prohibition trap created by its gigantic neighbor.

As Iain Young makes very clear, Canadian media and politicians must assert Canadian sovereignty and explicitly denounce the counterproductive fraud of marijuana prohibition. Major Canadian papers have already made some very bold statements.

They must make clear that they are defending the freedom of the Canadian people.

Canada will also be making a major contribution to the freedom of the people of the world.)
